## ⭐ THE TREE — which owner each hole answers to (Brian, 2026-07-31)

```
SEED (the three owners)              ROOTS (their disciplines)

owner-1 · documentation format  ──▶  doc-planning · doc-structure           🆕
owner-2 · development           ──▶  dev-database · dev-backend · dev-frontend
owner-3 · functional-flow       ──▶  val-functional · val-integration       🆕
```

> **Brian, correcting the AI:** *"los expertise eran formato de documentación, desarrollador,
> validación de flujo funcional. Los 3 que pusiste van DENTRO de desarrollador — es una división
> como si fuera un árbol."*

**What changed:** the AI had presented database/backend/frontend at the same level as the owners.
They are owner-2's **branches**. Correcting it exposed a real asymmetry — owner-1 and owner-3 had
**no disciplines at all**, so they judged with no body of criterion of their own. Their four
files were created on 2026-07-31 (structure + wiring; criterion still Brian's).

**Filenames carry the `<owner>-<discipline>` prefix** so the tree is visible in `ls` — a flat list
of seven files hides which owner each one answers to, which is how the confusion started.

## 3 · THE METHOD FOR FILLING THEM

> 🔴 **The AI asks. Brian answers with real cases. The AI structures.**
> **Never** *"the AI drafts and Brian corrects"* — a draft written first comes out as
> *"use best practices"*, which is as empty as *"it is fine"*.

Recorded as **risk #1 of phase F1** in the implementation plan.

**Format:** one discipline per session · 6-8 questions · the questions are already written at the
bottom of each file.

**Suggested order:** `principles/expertise/dev-database.md` first — it is where Brian has already expressed the most
criterion, and it is what propagates the most.

---

## 4 · HOW TO KNOW A HOLE IS WELL FILLED

| ✅ Good criterion | ⛔ Empty criterion |
|---|---|
| *"a default never points at something that has an owner"* | *"use good defaults"* |
| *"those values must live in the DB, not in code, so a mistake does not require a push"* | *"avoid hardcoding"* |
| *"if the state does not survive a refresh, it is not done"* | *"handle state properly"* |

> **The test:** could a script or a checklist verify it? If it cannot be checked, it is not criterion
> yet — it is an intention.
